messages:
Nina (support): Heads-up — customer Alice on Private reported intermittent KMS decrypt failures and a latency/retry billing spike right after they rotated their CMK. Error in logs: `InvalidCiphertextException: EncryptionContextMismatch`. cc @Harry @Kevin

Alice (customer): Seeing ~0.7% of requests fail with 403-ish KMS errors, other requests succeed. No app code change, only a scheduled key rotation. We sent logs + request IDs.

sre-bot: :rotating_light: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-3289 (priority P2) — automated aggregation attached.

Harry (eng-security): Can you paste the smallest repro (request headers/payload) and the KMS error block? Also which assume-role/STS flow they use (cross-account role chaining?)

Nina (support): Paste from customer logs (sanitized):
```
2026-05-02T10:12:43Z requestId=abc123 KMS.Decrypt Failed InvalidCiphertextException EncryptionContextMismatch {"expected": {"user_id":"acct-9876","env":"prod","session":"ey..."}, "provided": {"user_id":"acct-9876","env":"prod"}}
2026-05-02T10:12:43Z retried
2026-05-02T10:12:44Z requestId=def456 KMS.Decrypt OK latency=120ms
```
They show the provided encryption context truncated compared to expected. Customer uses an internal proxy in our Private deployment that forwards requests to AWS KMS (cross-account). They also do role chaining: app -> infra-role -> kms-proxy-role (assume-role twice).

Kevin (infra): Role chaining + session policy + headers can be a problem. If the proxy serializes the full encryption context into a header or signs it into a session token, some proxies or ALBs can truncate long headers. We had a similar-but-not-identical flap in another account where the `x-redwood-encctx` header got truncated to ~4k. KMS expects exact match.

Harry (eng-security): Agreed. Quick checklist: 1) confirm the raw KMS Encrypt context produced by client pre-rotate; 2) verify the proxy preserves the full context bytes to the exact KMS API call; 3) check if STS AssumeRole session policy or principal restrictions strip context. Also: which AWS SDK language and version? Some SDKs had a bug where they drop null/empty context keys.

Nina (support): Repro steps the customer provided: 1) call our API CreateKey (we forward to their AWS CMK via proxy) 2) rotate CMK via AWS console 3) send production traffic (same code) 4) ~0.5-1% decrypts fail. They attached a curl that reproduces when run in their env.

Alice (customer): Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." \
  -H "X-EncCtx: {\"user_id\":\"acct-9876\",\"env\":\"prod\",\"session\":\"<long-jwt-ish>\"}" \
  https://private.redwood.example/v1/decrypt
```
They said dropping the `session` field in the encctx makes the failure go away. The `session` string is ~2800 chars.

Kevin (infra): That screams header-size truncation. ALB and some proxies drop or truncate large headers. KMS encryption context size limit (docs) is smallish (4096 bytes total? need to confirm). If the proxy truncates, AWS returns EncryptionContextMismatch because the CMK ciphertext was created with full context.

Harry (eng-security): Immediate mitigations: - Tell customer to avoid storing long session tokens in encryption context (shorten or hash them). - Add a temporary fallback: try Decrypt with truncated context then Decrypt without context? Note: KMS won't decrypt if encryption context doesn't match; trying without context will also fail if context was used at encrypt time. So fallback won't help unless you have prior plaintext or a re-encrypt path.

Nina (support): Customer asked for a hotfix on our side because they can't change token length quickly. They want us to ensure our Private proxy preserves the full header and does not re-encode or base64+split in a way that triggers truncation.

Kevin (infra): Actionable immediate steps from infra: 1) check Private proxy logs for header sizes for that customer (we log header lengths). 2) enable passthrough mode for the `X-EncCtx` header for that tenant (config flag) — low risk. 3) add a temporary request-size metric alarm so we can alert on truncation.

Harry (eng-security): Longer-term: 1) Add validation on our side that rejects or warns on long encryption-context values at ingest time (fail early). 2) Provide a migration helper that lets customers hash/derive a short `encctx_id` linked to server-side mapping (we can store a mapping encrypted with customer's CMK). 3) Document best practices: avoid embedding large session tokens in encryption context.

Nina (support): Customer is ok with a passthrough toggle as immediate relief. They also opened an AWS support case (SR-9876543) to confirm KMS limits.

Alice (customer): Thanks — toggled passthrough worked in our staging after Kevin flipped it. We saw failure rate drop to 0.0% in a 10k request sample. Can you please keep the passthrough enabled until we roll a shorter token?

Kevin (infra): Passthrough will remain enabled for that tenant, I've opened INF-2026-614 to track tech debt. Also adding unit test to ensure header copying doesn't base64-wrap and exceed LB limits.

Harry (eng-security): I'll draft a short KB entry for customers on encryption-context size limits, role chaining caveats, and our passthrough toggle. Also adding a checklist item for KMS key rotation runbooks to verify proxy header integrity.

Nina (support): Closing loop with customer and marking INC-2026-3289 as "mitigated by config toggle". We'll follow up once KB + infra patch done. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
